transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. what's been in your dreams lately?
oh hey! i had a really weird one the other day, it stuck with me.
those are the best kind. what happened?
it was this tiny train station in the middle of a desert. nothing else around, just sand everywhere
a train station all alone out there. that's strange in a good way. what did it look like?
like a comic book, like thick black lines and flat colours. the sun was straight overhead so every shadow was a hard black shape
i can see that. the shadows would be so stark. were you waiting for a train, or just there?
yeah, waiting for a train. there was just a bench and a clock on a pole, nothing else on the platform
a clock on a pole. did you notice the time on it?
i looked at it and it was melting, dripping down the pole like wax. so no, couldn't really read it
melting. and you were just waiting there with it. what did that feel like?
weirdly calm, like it wasn't surprising at all. but also kind of lonely since it was so empty
calm and lonely at the same time. that's a particular feeling. was there anything you wanted to do while you waited?
not really, just stood there. but an old man in a white suit was sitting on the bench, with a camel standing next to him, completely calm
a camel just standing there like it's normal. do you remember anything about the old man?
he told me the train was late, like it always was. that's all i remember
for you, or in the dream?
in the dream, he said it out loud to me. he didn't seem annoyed about it or anything
so the train being late was just a fact of the place. that fits with the town being so still. was there any sound in the dream?
i heard a train whistle far away, but no train came. after that the old man and the camel got up and walked off into the desert
they just walked out into the sand. that feels like the right way for that station to work. did you leave too, or stay behind?
i stayed on the platform, watching them get smaller and smaller. then i woke up
just watching them go. and were you you in the dream, or was it like seeing it all from somewhere else?
i was me, standing there. i could feel the heat of the sun even though it looked flat like a drawing
so the air had weight even while the scene looked like a comic. that's a strange mix. what did the heat feel like, exactly?
like that kind of dry, pressing heat where you just don't want to move much. it made everything feel slow
i can imagine that. the dream started with you going there—do you remember how it began?
no, i don't remember how i got there. it just started with me already on the platform
of course. dreams work like that. was there anything else around you, or was it just the bench, the clock, and the two of them?
just the bench, the clock, and them. the sand went on forever in every direction, no other buildings
so no station building even, just the platform. that's really stripped down. did anything about it remind you of somewhere you've seen before?
not that i can think of. it didn't feel like a real place i'd been, more like a picture of a place
a picture of a place, yeah. and yet you could feel the heat of it. when that old man said the train was late, did his voice sound like anyone you know?
i don't remember his voice being like anyone i know. it was just a calm, sort of stating-it voice

so you were on a tiny platform in the middle of the desert, just you, a bench, and a melting clock on a pole. it looked like a comic, flat with thick black lines and the sun straight overhead so every shadow was a hard black shape. an old man in a white suit sat on the bench with a camel standing next to him. he said the train was late, like it always was. you heard a train whistle far away but no train came. then he and the camel got up and walked off into the sand, getting smaller, and you stayed behind, feeling that dry pressing heat and a calm loneliness.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah, that's exactly right. nothing's missing
that's your dream, then. would you like to see it drawn?
yes, i would

there are a few ways we could draw this.

a bold comic with flat colours, crisp and graphic like a panel from a comic book. a faded screenprint, worn like an old poster left too long in the sun. a stark black-and-white woodcut, everything reduced to bold black marks against the white page. a photograph, a scene that looks real but with the flatness of a comic and the weight of the heat. which of these feels closest to your dream, or would you describe it your own way?
the bold comic with flat colours, for sure

i'll start with you, then, in that bold flat colour comic.

and since you were standing right there in it, i'll draw you too. would you like to be drawn as you are—you can tell me a little about yourself—or however i imagine you?
however you imagine me is fine

okay, i'll imagine you. i'm sketching you and the old man and the camel and the tiny train station now. everything's being drawn and will appear on the right over the next minute or two. once it's there, tell me if anything looks off.
the one with the old man and camel walking away looks right, just them getting smaller on the sand. the others too
i'm glad. that's the dream, then—just the way you remember it.
yeah, it really does look like it. the flat colours and black shadows are spot on
i'll draw the moments of the dream in order, each one carrying on from the ones before it. they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
okay, i'll wait for the rest
good, i'll keep drawing then.
no rush, take your time
no rush at all. the rest of the moments are still coming, they'll show up on the right in a bit.
the one with the melting clock is right, it's dripping down the pole just like that

yeah, it's got that slow drip to it.

and the one where the old man in the white suit is just sitting on the bench with the camel next to him—does that look the way you remember it?
yeah, he looks calm like that, and the camel does too. the black outline around them is right
the black outline does a lot of the work, yeah. the rest of the moments are still being drawn, they'll show up on the right soon.
okay, i'll keep an eye out

now the moment where the old man tells you the train is late is up, too.

does that look the way you remember it?
it mostly does, but in that one the old man and camel are still on the bench, not getting up yet

ah, right, they're still just sitting there on the bench, not getting up yet.

i'll redraw that moment with them still sitting like that, and it'll appear on the right in a moment.
thanks, that one was a bit off otherwise

no problem at all. i've kept that moment with them still sitting on the bench, not getting up yet.

the other moments are still being drawn. if anything else feels off, just tell me and i'll fix it.
